title: Ops Architect — gut notes + provisional scorecard
body:
Short context:
- Loop: Ops Architect (infra + runtime stability). 60-minute pairing + 45-minute behavioral loop on 2026-02-27. Me + Ilya + Samira in the loop; Noor taking these notes for later synth.

Immediate first impressions (raw):
- Confident operator energy, pragmatic trade-off framing. Comfortable with ambiguity; often steered conversations to recovery plans and SLOs rather than purely theoretical fixes.
- Strong incident storytelling: concrete examples of undiagnosed memory leaks and how they constrained rollout windows. Used postmortems as a lever for process change (oncall rotation tweaks, postmortem accountability).
- System design chops are solid for monolith-to-microservice decomposition and for building staging-rehearsal pipelines; showed good intuition for KV cache eviction effects on downstream compaction.
- Some gaps in LLM-specific inference nuance: less familiar with KV-cache internals at transformer-level (we probed quantization/kv layout) — they asked clarifying Qs and leaned on team assumptions. Could partner well but would need short ramp on model runtime internals.

Provisional scorecard (my private calibration):
- Production reliability mindset: 5/5 — clear examples and proposals for safeguards (canary + automated rollback + traffic mirroring).
- Troubleshooting & debugging: 4/5 — strong, but relies more on process than low-level kernel debugging.
- System design (scalability & cost): 4/5 — good capacity planning instincts, creative costing ideas (dynamic burst lanes, preemptible fallback).
- LLM infra domain knowledge: 2.5/5 — limited hands-on with KV cache internals, quantization tradeoffs; able to learn but will take time.
- Communication & leadership: 4.5/5 — succinct, aligns cross-functional teams, good at writing incident comms in examples.
- Culture/values fit: 4/5 — pragmatic, engineering-first, leans into ownership.

Strengths (evidence):
- Story about a week-long outage traced to a GC edge case; they led a 3-day orthogonal rollout (traffic shaping + hotfix) and instituted a nightly quick-scan job that surfaced the memory trend early. Demonstrates ownership across plan->execute->process-change.
- Brought up cost attribution per feature and built a simple dashboard in their previous role using tagging + signal decomposition. Practical and measurable.
- Pairing exercise: designed a resilient ingress path for a model serving fleet with tiered routing. Good trade-offs for latency vs. cost.

Concerns / risk flags:
- Low familiarity with model-level optimizer kernels (no direct hands-on with Triton/FlashAttention/llama.cpp niches). If we hire at senior level expecting domain depth, this is a risk. Consider hiring as "Ops Architect (Platform)" rather than inference kernel specialist.
- When pressed on long-tail failure modes (KV cache corruption across hosts), defaulted to broad mitigations (draining + repro) rather than proposing stricter end-to-end verification or checksums. Not necessarily a blocker but a gap.
- Past org size: has mostly worked in 50-200 person companies. Scaling to 1000+ customer SLA mindset is new territory (they expressed excitement but had less explicit experience with enterprise SLAs and compliance audits).

Take-home assessment summary (they submitted a short design doc):
- Doc quality: concise and readable, prioritized SLOs, rollout plan, and a lightweight observability map. Missing: concrete metrics/thresholds for auto-rollbacks and no explicit cost model of the proposed caching layer.
- Rough grade: B+; shows strong operational instincts but needs more domain numbers.

Pairing session notes (what we did and their approach):
- Prompt: design a tiered serving path with best-effort fast lane (low context) and high-quality delayed lane (high-context) with graceful fallback.
- Approach: decomposed by ingress, routing policy, cache warmup, and fallback. Proposed a lightweight per-request budget token to decide lane. Liked that because it is incremental and observable.
- Missed: explicit per-token billing impact and how to credit-borrow across lanes. We flagged that and they took notes as an action item.

Suggested leveling & ramp plan (sketch):
- Hire level: Senior (IC4) / Ops Architect (platform-focused) — not senior inference researcher.
- 0-30 days: onboarding to runtime repo, read our top 3 LPs (KV cache, batching, routing), pair with runtime engineer on a 1-week bug triage rotation.
- 30-90 days: own a small SLA surface (one model + one region), deliver an improved alerting rule and a mitigation playbook, present a post-launch blameless retro.

Recommended next steps (my vote):
- Move to hiring manager sync + one domain deep-dive loop specifically on KV cache and quantization assumptions. Have a runtime engineer who knows the code run the loop (Ilya recommended).
- If we see reasonable openness and concrete learning plan in that loop, extend an offer at Senior IC level. Otherwise close.

Questions for the next loop (to resolve hiring decision):
- Can they explain a KV cache evict/corruption scenario end-to-end with proposed detection mechanisms (checksums, per-batch verifiers)?
- Have them walk through a concrete quantization failure mode (e.g., 4-bit overflow) and proposed monitoring signatures.
- Org scaling: ask about one enterprise SLA they've owned end-to-end and the hardest compliance ask they had to solve.

Admin notes / followups I owe:
- Share this doc with Ilya & Samira (already added them as collaborators).
- Create a short debrief message for hiring manager + recruiter summarizing the gap areas and recommended level.
- Add JIRA/loop notes: put a small ticket for domain-deep-dive-loop and tag runtime-eng.

Personal heuristics (why I lean hire):
- We need someone who will prioritize reliability and playbook-driven incident reduction. Candidate has strong track record there and will likely raise baseline.
- The model-internal skills are trainable in ~8-12 weeks with concentrated pairing; the harder-to-teach thing is the ownership and discipline — they have it.

Unresolved feelings / instincts to watch:
- They are very process-forward; sometimes I worry about over-optimizing process vs. shipping small, pragmatic code changes. Watch velocity in first 60 days.
- Cultural fit with runtime team seems positive; Samira mentioned they were slightly more "ops-skeptical" during behavioral loop but warmed up in pairing.

Bottom line (one-liner):
- Strong Senior Ops Architect candidate with excellent incident ownership and platform instincts; hire for platform-facing reliability role, add a short technical loop to validate model-runtime specifics before final offer.
